title: Paper Feed Motor Error
shortDescription: The paper feed motor has failed or is not responding to commands.
fullDescription:
Error code 000020 on Epson printers indicates a failure in the paper feed motor system. This motor drives the rollers that transport paper through the print zone. When the motor cannot start or maintain proper speed, the printer cannot advance paper.

The error can be caused by a mechanical obstruction preventing the motor from turning, a failed motor, a motor driver circuit failure on the main board, or excessive load from jammed paper.

This is a more serious error than a simple paper jam, as it indicates the motor system itself is not functioning rather than just paper being stuck.

causes.cause: Paper jam creating excessive motor load

symptoms: Error 000020 on display or status monitor

fixSteps.title: Clear All Paper
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer, remove all paper from trays, and check inside for any jammed paper. Remove any debris.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the printer for 5 minutes to reset motor controller. Plug back in and power on.

fixSteps.title: Check Feed Path
fixSteps.instruction: Open all access doors and manually check that internal rollers turn freely. Remove any obstructions.

fixSteps.title: Listen for Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Power on with no paper loaded and listen for motor operation. If silence where motor sound should be, the motor may need replacement.

whenToCallPro: If the motor or motor driver circuit has failed, professional board-level or motor replacement is required.

faq.q: Is this different from a paper jam error?
faq.a: Yes, 000020 specifically indicates a motor problem, not just stuck paper. A regular jam uses codes like E-03.

faq.q: Can I hear if the motor is working?
faq.a: Yes, during printer initialization you should hear the feed motor engage. Complete silence from the feed area suggests motor failure.

title: Ink System Charging Error
shortDescription: The ink system failed to complete the initial charging process.
fullDescription:
Error code 000036 on Epson printers indicates the ink charging system could not complete its cycle. Ink charging is the process of filling the ink delivery tubes from the cartridges or tanks to the printhead during initial setup or after cartridge replacement.

This error is common on Epson EcoTank models where ink must travel from external tanks through long tubes to reach the printhead. Air bubbles in the tubes, low ink levels, or a clogged ink delivery path can prevent successful charging.

The charging process is essential for priming the printhead with ink. Without successful charging, the printer cannot produce any output.

causes.cause: Ink tanks not filled to required level

symptoms: Long charging time followed by error

fixSteps.title: Check Ink Levels
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all ink tanks are filled to the upper line. Refill any tanks that are below the lower line with genuine Epson ink.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer, wait 5 minutes, then turn on. The charging process will restart automatically.

fixSteps.title: Run Power Cleaning
fixSteps.instruction: If the printer allows access to maintenance functions, run Power Cleaning to force ink through the system with higher pressure.

fixSteps.title: Check for Kinked Tubes
fixSteps.instruction: If visible, inspect the ink tubes from tanks to printhead. Ensure none are kinked, pinched, or have visible air gaps.

whenToCallPro: If the ink pump has failed or the internal ink delivery system is blocked beyond what cleaning can resolve.

faq.q: How long does initial charging take?
faq.a: Initial ink charging on EcoTank models typically takes 10-20 minutes. This is normal and uses a significant amount of ink.

faq.q: Why does charging use so much ink?
faq.a: The initial charge fills the entire ink delivery system from tanks to printhead, including all internal tubes. This is a one-time high ink usage.

title: Printhead Carriage Error
shortDescription: The printhead carriage is stuck or obstructed and cannot move.
fullDescription:
Error 0xF1 on Epson printers indicates the printhead carriage cannot move along its track. This error is similar to errors on other brands where the carriage mechanism is blocked or jammed.

The carriage must travel freely from left to right on a guide rail. Paper jams, foreign objects, dried ink buildup on the rail, or a failed carriage motor can all prevent proper movement.

This error halts all printing until the obstruction is cleared. The carriage motor is protected by the firmware and will stop attempting to move if resistance is detected, to prevent damage.

causes.cause: Paper or debris blocking carriage path

fixSteps.title: Power Off and Check Carriage
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and unplug the printer. Open the top cover and gently try to move the printhead carriage left and right by hand. Note any resistance.

fixSteps.title: Remove Obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Remove any paper scraps, packing material, or foreign objects from the carriage path. Check behind and underneath the carriage.

fixSteps.title: Clean Carriage Rail
fixSteps.instruction: Use a lint-free cloth dampened with a small amount of light machine oil to lubricate the metal carriage rail. Wipe off excess.

fixSteps.title: Check Carriage Belt
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the rubber belt that drives the carriage. If it appears loose, cracked, or has slipped off a pulley, professional repair is needed.

whenToCallPro: If the carriage belt is broken or the carriage motor has failed, professional repair is required.

faq.q: Can I move the carriage by hand?
faq.a: Yes, with the printer unplugged. Gently slide it left and right. If it moves freely, the obstruction may be intermittent.
On most Epson consumer printers, belt replacement requires significant disassembly and is best left to professionals.

title: Carriage Encoder Error
shortDescription: The printhead carriage encoder cannot be read, preventing accurate positioning.
fullDescription:
Error code 000033 on Epson printers indicates the carriage encoder system has failed. The encoder system consists of a thin transparent strip with fine markings and an optical sensor on the carriage that reads these markings to determine precise carriage position.

When the encoder cannot be read accurately, the printer cannot position the printhead correctly for printing. This results in misaligned output or complete inability to print.

The encoder strip can become contaminated with ink mist over time, or it can be physically displaced from its mounting clips. In rare cases, the optical sensor on the carriage itself may fail.

causes.cause: Encoder strip contaminated with ink mist
Encoder strip displaced from mounting clips

symptoms: Error 000033 on display or status monitor

fixSteps.title: Locate Encoder Strip
fixSteps.instruction: Open the printer cover. Look for a thin transparent plastic strip running horizontally behind the carriage. It has very fine vertical lines printed on it.

fixSteps.title: Clean Encoder Strip
fixSteps.instruction: Gently hold the strip with one hand and wipe it with a lint-free cloth slightly dampened with distilled water. Wipe along the length of the strip, not across it.

fixSteps.title: Check Mounting Clips
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the encoder strip is properly seated in its plastic mounting clips at both ends. If a clip has released, gently reattach the strip.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle and Test
fixSteps.instruction: After cleaning, turn the printer off and on. Print a test page to verify carriage positioning is accurate.

whenToCallPro: If the encoder strip is torn or the optical sensor has failed, professional replacement is needed.

faq.q: Can I buy a replacement encoder strip?
faq.a: Yes, encoder strips are available as spare parts online. Match the part number to your specific printer model.

faq.q: How do I prevent encoder contamination?
faq.a: Regular printing keeps ink mist to a minimum. Printers in dusty environments may benefit from occasional encoder strip cleaning.

fixSteps.instruction: Lightly wipe the clear plastic strip behind the carriage with a damp lint-free cloth (water only).

fixSteps.title: Inspect Home Sensor

whenToCallPro: Damaged or torn encoder strips require service replacement.

faq.a: Yes — if the head can't park, ink dries within hours.

title: Print Head Capping Station Error

symptoms: Print head not sealing audibly when parked

fixSteps.title: Clean Capping Station

fixSteps.title: Run Head Cleaning

fixSteps.title: Service Capping Mechanism
fixSteps.instruction: If error returns, the cap mechanism needs service.

whenToCallPro: Persistent capping issues lead to permanent head damage — service quickly.

faq.a: Tap water minerals can crystallize on rubber and worsen the seal.

title: Mainboard Communication Error

fixSteps.title: Dry the Connector

fixSteps.title: Replace Mainboard

faq.a: Often — Epsons left in damp basements develop 0xC1 over time.

title: Pump Motor / Maintenance Station Error
shortDescription: The maintenance pump motor that primes the print head has failed.
fullDescription: Epson error 0xEA indicates a fault in the pump motor located in the cleaning/maintenance station. The pump pulls ink through the head during cleaning cycles. A failed pump leads to head-cleaning errors and eventually print-quality collapse.

causes.cause: Pump motor seized from dried ink
Failed motor driver on logic board

symptoms: Audible grinding or no sound during head cleaning
Print quality severely degraded with banding

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off via the power button, wait 60 seconds, power on. A transient stall sometimes clears.

fixSteps.title: Inspect maintenance station
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and unplug. Open the right-side cover, locate the cap/pump assembly, and look for thick dried ink around the cap.

fixSteps.title: Soften ink with distilled water
fixSteps.instruction: Apply distilled water with a syringe (no IPA on caps) and let soak 5 minutes. Wipe excess gently.

fixSteps.title: Replace the pump assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If the pump is mechanically failed, replace the maintenance assembly with the part number for your specific Epson model.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement is service-level on Epson. If contacts and seals appear fine but the motor will not turn, an authorized technician should replace the assembly.

faq.a: No — 0xEA means the pump itself is broken, so cleaning cycles cannot run. The pump must be repaired before cleanings will work.

title: Carriage (CR) Motor Error
shortDescription: The carriage motor that drives the print head left-and-right has failed or stalled.
fullDescription: Epson error 0xF1 indicates a fault in the CR (carriage) motor or its position-encoder feedback. The printer cannot reliably move the head and halts. Causes include a stuck carriage, a torn encoder strip, or a failed motor.

causes.cause: Carriage stuck on debris or dried ink

symptoms: Grinding or skipping noise on power-up

fixSteps.title: Power off and free the carriage
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off, open the cover, and gently move the carriage by hand from edge to edge. Find and remove any obstructions.

fixSteps.title: Clean the encoder strip
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the clear plastic strip behind the carriage with a lint-free cloth and distilled water. Look for tears or scratches that would require replacement.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the belt
fixSteps.instruction: Slide the carriage and watch the timing belt for slipping or fraying. A loose belt may need tensioning or replacement.

fixSteps.title: Service motor or belt
fixSteps.instruction: Belt or motor replacement is service work on most Epson models. Engage Epson service or an authorized repair center.

whenToCallPro: Belt and motor work is service-level on Epson printers; user repair beyond cleaning is rarely successful.

faq.q: How can I tell if the encoder strip is the issue?
faq.a: If the carriage moves but stops at random positions and produces vertical banding, the encoder strip is the prime suspect.

title: Paper Feed (PF) Motor Error
shortDescription: The paper-feed motor that advances paper through the printer has failed or is being blocked.
fullDescription: Epson error 0xF3 is a fault in the PF (paper feed) motor or its rotary encoder. The motor either failed mechanically, is being mechanically blocked, or its position encoder cannot be read.

causes.cause: Paper jam in the feed path
Stripped feed gear or worn motor
Failed motor driver on logic board

symptoms: Paper not advancing or advancing erratically
Whining noise from rear of printer

fixSteps.title: Clear paper path
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, open all covers and the rear panel. Remove any stuck sheets, scraps, or staples.

fixSteps.title: Clean the encoder wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the small clear/striped disc on the PF roller shaft. Wipe gently with a lint-free cloth — no liquid.

fixSteps.title: Run nozzle check after recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Power on and run a nozzle-check page to confirm normal feed.

fixSteps.title: Service motor/gear if persistent
fixSteps.instruction: If the encoder is clean and path is clear, the motor or feed gear is suspect — service-level repair.

whenToCallPro: If the path is clear and encoder cleaned but 0xF3 returns, the PF motor or its driver IC has failed; engage Epson service.

faq.a: No — 0xF3 is mechanical/feed; head cleaning routines do not touch the PF motor.

title: Paper Jam Detected
shortDescription: Paper has jammed somewhere along the paper path.
fullDescription: Epson error 0x10 is the generic paper-jam code. The paper-position sensor sees paper where there should be none, or fails to see it where it should be, after a feed attempt. Resolution requires removing the jam and verifying the path.
symptoms: 0x10 on the LCD with paper visible inside

fixSteps.title: Pull the jammed sheet
fixSteps.instruction: Open the front and rear covers, and gently pull the sheet in the direction of paper travel — never against it.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for fragments
fixSteps.instruction: Use a flashlight to check the path for torn pieces, especially around rollers and sensor flags.

fixSteps.title: Clean the pickup roller
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the rubber feed roller with a lint-free cloth dampened with distilled water; allow to dry.

fixSteps.title: Replace pickup roller if multifeeding
fixSteps.instruction: Persistent jams from a glazed roller require replacement of the pickup-roller kit for your model.

whenToCallPro: If the path is fully clear and rollers are new but 0x10 persists, a sensor is suspect — service the printer.

faq.a: Most often a small fragment is left behind, or a glazed pickup roller is multi-feeding sheets that catch on each other downstream.

title: Fatal Error / Logic Board Issue
shortDescription: Epson reports a fatal internal error — typically a logic-board or main controller fault.
fullDescription: Error 0x97 is Epson's general fatal error. It indicates the main board has detected an unrecoverable internal fault — often the head driver, main controller, or power supply failing. Most consumer 0x97 cases end in printer replacement.

causes.cause: Failed head driver IC on main board

symptoms: Printer cycles but never reaches Ready

fixSteps.title: Power off for 5 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect from power for 5 minutes to discharge capacitors. Reconnect and power on.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If the printer reaches a state where firmware update is possible, install the latest from the Epson support page for your model.

fixSteps.title: Service evaluation
fixSteps.instruction: Bring the printer to authorized Epson service to diagnose between board, head driver, and power-supply failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace if uneconomical
fixSteps.instruction: On most consumer Epson models, the repair cost exceeds replacement value; consider a new printer.

whenToCallPro: 0x97 is almost always a board-level fault. Engage Epson service or compare repair quote to replacement cost before proceeding.

faq.a: Realistically no — it is a logic-board class fault. Firmware re-flashing is the only user-level option and rarely succeeds.

title: Service Required - Waste Ink Pad Counter
shortDescription: Epson's waste-ink pad counter has reached or exceeded its service limit.
fullDescription: Error 0x9A indicates the waste-ink pad counter has reached the service limit. The printer locks to prevent ink overflow inside the chassis. The fix is to replace the pads and reset the counter using Epson's Adjustment Program (service tool).

causes.cause: Excessive head cleanings shortening pad life
Premature counter trigger from firmware update

symptoms: Printer refuses to print until reset
Ink-stained pads visible at the rear maintenance hatch

fixSteps.title: Stop using the printer
fixSteps.instruction: Continued cycling without reset risks an internal ink leak. Power off until ready to service.

fixSteps.title: Plan service or DIY
fixSteps.instruction: Authorized Epson service replaces pads and resets via service tool. DIY users can buy replacement pads and use Epson's Adjustment Program to reset.

fixSteps.title: Replace pads
fixSteps.instruction: Open the rear maintenance area, remove old pads (wear gloves), insert new pads.

fixSteps.title: Reset counter
fixSteps.instruction: Run Adjustment Program / service tool, select Waste Ink Pad Counter, and reset. Power-cycle to confirm clear.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable opening the printer or sourcing the Adjustment Program, an authorized Epson service center will perform the pad service.

faq.q: Is 0x9A a real failure or a counter?
faq.a: It is a counter-driven service hold. Pads do reach a saturation point eventually, but the counter often locks the printer before a real overflow.

title: Paper Feed Warning - Cassette
shortDescription: Paper failed to feed from the cassette tray.
fullDescription: Warning W-01 on Epson printers means the paper-feed sensor expected to see paper after a feed attempt and did not. It is generally a soft warning — clear and reload — but persistent W-01 points to a worn pickup roller or wrong paper-size setting.

causes.cause: Paper not loaded or below sensor
Paper guides not snug against stack

symptoms: W-01 on display when starting print
Cassette pulls in but paper does not advance
Frequent recurrence with light or curled paper

fixSteps.title: Reload paper correctly
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all paper, fan a stack of 20-30 sheets, square the edges, and reload. Slide guides snug.

fixSteps.title: Match driver to paper size
fixSteps.instruction: In the Epson driver, set the source to Cassette and select the same size loaded.

fixSteps.title: Clean pickup roller
fixSteps.instruction: Use the printer's automatic Bottom Plate Cleaning routine, or wipe the rubber roller with a damp lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace pickup roller
fixSteps.instruction: If feeds remain unreliable after cleaning, install the model-specific roller kit.

whenToCallPro: If a fresh roller and correct settings still produce W-01, the paper-out sensor or feed motor may need service.

faq.q: Is W-01 the same as a paper jam?
faq.a: No — W-01 is 'no paper detected' (or feed failure); a jam is paper stuck mid-path. They have different sensor sources.

title: Paper Feed Warning - Rear/Manual Feed
shortDescription: Paper failed to feed from the rear or manual feed slot.
fullDescription: Warning W-02 on Epson printers indicates the rear/manual feed source did not advance paper as expected. The rear feed often handles specialty media (envelopes, photo paper), so causes include incorrect media-type setting, paper that is too thick, or a worn rear-feed roller.

causes.cause: Paper-type setting does not match media

symptoms: Envelope or photo paper not picked
Skewed or jammed feed when paper does advance

fixSteps.title: Verify media-type setting
fixSteps.instruction: In the print driver, set Paper Type to match exactly (e.g., Envelope, Glossy Photo). Set Source to Rear/Manual.

fixSteps.title: Insert paper correctly
fixSteps.instruction: Place media against the right guide, slide the left guide snug. For envelopes, follow the orientation marking on the rear feed.

fixSteps.title: Decurl photo paper
fixSteps.instruction: If photo paper is curled, gently flatten with even pressure or store flat overnight.

fixSteps.title: Service the rear-feed roller
fixSteps.instruction: If a fresh stack still does not feed, the rear-feed roller may be worn — schedule service.

whenToCallPro: If the rear feed remains unreliable across paper types, the rear-feed mechanism likely needs service or replacement parts.

faq.q: Can I print envelopes from the cassette instead?
faq.a: Most Epson models route envelopes only through the rear/manual feed; consult your specific manual for cassette envelope support.

title: Low Ink Information
shortDescription: The printer is informing you that one or more ink levels are running low.
fullDescription: Information code I-50 is an advisory, not a fault. It tells you ink levels are reaching reorder thresholds. The printer continues to operate, but EcoTank/WorkForce models may show this with the colour identified. Replace cartridges or refill the appropriate tank when convenient.
symptoms: I-50 with affected colour shown on the panel

fixSteps.title: Identify the low colour
fixSteps.instruction: On the panel or Epson Status Monitor, note which cartridge or tank is low.

fixSteps.title: Order or refill
fixSteps.instruction: For cartridge models, have a replacement on hand. For EcoTank, refill from the matching colour bottle following the panel guidance.

fixSteps.title: Replace cartridge or fill tank
fixSteps.instruction: When ink runs out, follow the printer's prompts to install a new cartridge or fill the EcoTank to the upper line.

fixSteps.title: Reset levels (EcoTank only)
fixSteps.instruction: After filling, confirm/reset the ink levels on the panel as prompted.

whenToCallPro: I-50 is information only — no service is needed unless a refilled tank still reports low ink, which suggests a sensor issue.

faq.q: Can I keep printing through I-50?
faq.a: Yes — I-50 is informational. The printer halts only when a colour is fully depleted or another error is raised.

title: Printhead Temperature Out of Range
shortDescription: The printhead temperature sensor reported a value outside its operating range.
fullDescription: Epson error 0x9D indicates the printhead temperature is too high or too low for safe firing. Causes include continuous high-coverage printing without rest, a failed temperature sensor, or a dried head requiring extensive cleaning.

causes.cause: Ambient room temperature out of spec

fixSteps.title: Pause and let cool
fixSteps.instruction: Cancel any active job and let the printer sit for 30 minutes with power on (fans run during idle).

fixSteps.title: Verify ambient temperature
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the printer is operating in the manufacturer's specified ambient range (typically 10-35 deg C).

fixSteps.title: Reduce continuous load
fixSteps.instruction: Split very large jobs into batches and avoid back-to-back high-coverage prints.

fixSteps.title: Service the head
fixSteps.instruction: If 0x9D returns immediately on cold start, the head temperature sensor is suspect — service-level repair.

whenToCallPro: Persistent 0x9D after cool-down points to a failed temperature sensor inside the head, which is service-level repair.

faq.a: It is a protective halt — the printer is preventing damage to the head. Following the cool-down step is enough in normal cases.
